paragraphs: 🔥 EXPOSED: The Dark Web of Pandemic Profiteering — Pharmally, DepEd Laptops, Zaldy Co, and the Great Betrayal of the Filipino People 🔥
"You shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free." – John 8:32

Dear readers — what if I told you the greatest heist of your lifetime didn't happen at midnight, in the shadows of back alleys — but in plain sight, on government documents, televised press conferences, and COVID-era contracts? What if the real looters wore neckties, not ski masks? Buckle up. This is the full truth about the Pharmally Pharmaceutical scandal, the DepEd laptop corruption case, and their tangled links to a deeper system of abuse that’s still unraveling in 2025.
This isn't just news — this is the anatomy of betrayal.
This is your AHA moment. And you’ll never see government procurement the same way again.
PART I: PHARMALLY — PANDEMIC PROFITEERING AT PANIC SPEED

The year was 2020. COVID-19 hit the world like a divine judgment. Lockdowns spread, people were dying, masks vanished from shelves. And in that chaos, a company no one had ever heard of — Pharmally Pharmaceutical Corporation — suddenly became a multibillion-peso star.

Pharmally was a baby company, born in 2019. No track record. Paid-up capital of just ₱625,000. Yes, you read that right. Yet it bagged ₱11 billion+ in government contracts. Their supplies? Overpriced face masks, face shields, and test kits — some defective, others expired.
How?
The Shortcut: Government rules were suspended under emergency powers (Bayanihan Act). The Procurement Service–Department of Budget and Management (PS-DBM) did direct deals.
The Key Player: A certain Michael Yang, former Duterte economic adviser, was linked to Pharmally’s financiers. Senators asked: was Pharmally just a front for a Chinese-backed operation?
The Smoking Gun: Senate Blue Ribbon hearings in 2021–2022 exposed fraudulent deliveries, manipulated prices, and doctored documents. Senator Richard Gordon called it "state-sanctioned robbery."
And yet, even with all the facts exposed, prosecutions dragged. The Ombudsman even withdrew cases in 2025, pending "review." Why? You decide.
"Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light." – Isaiah 5:20
PART II: DEPED LAPTOPS — WHEN EDUCATION BECAME A CASH MACHINE

Flash forward to 2021. With schools closed, the government needed to help teachers teach online. The Department of Education (DepEd), through PS-DBM, bought laptops for public school teachers. Budget: ₱2.4 billion.

But the laptops were old, slow, and ridiculously overpriced — at ₱58,300 each. Tech experts cried foul. COA flagged the deal. Teachers cried — literally. These laptops couldn’t even run Zoom properly.
The supplier? Not yet proven to be the same as Pharmally — but connected players were involved. And one name popped up again: Christopher Lao — a DBM official involved in both cases.
The Fallout:
2022: Senate investigates.
2023: COA releases audit report confirming overpricing.
2024: DepEd, DBM, and PS officials suspended.
2025: Graft charges filed against ex-DepEd Secretary Leonor Briones, Christopher Lao, and 12 others.
Now, the latest?
As of November 2025, the Ombudsman reaffirmed charges against Briones and Lao after internal pressure from educators’ groups, citing public interest as “compelling and urgent.”
"My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge." – Hosea 4:6
PART III: THE ZALDY CO CONNECTION – A SYMPHONY OF SCANDALS

You want a master conductor? Enter Rep. Zaldy Co. Former Appropriations Committee chair. He allegedly helped push budget insertions that led to these shady deals — including contracts tied to his own companies, like Sunwest Construction.
Senate Majority Leader Villanueva said: Zaldy Co's firms were linked to both the Pharmally and DepEd deals.
But the latest scandal? As of November 2025:
Zaldy Co faces three Sandiganbayan criminal cases involving a ₱289 million ghost flood-control project in Oriental Mindoro.
Arrest warrants were issued on Nov 21, 2025, for Co and 17 others.
Allegations claim entire infrastructures were either nonexistent or collapsed shortly after ribbon-cuttings.
And wait — there’s more. Whistleblowers from DPWH and DepEd claim Zaldy Co’s office had pre-arranged “winning” contractors for multi-agency bids.
Now that’s not just corruption. That’s a franchise.
PART IV: WHAT'S REALLY WRONG HERE?
1. Legal Loophole Manipulation – Emergency procurement laws were weaponized. No public bidding. No transparency.
2. Shell Companies & Ghost Suppliers – Pharmally, laptop contractors — all had red flags: minimal capital, no experience, mysterious foreign backers.
3. Budget Insertion Cartels – Legislators allegedly steer money to departments where accomplices wait with pre-selected suppliers.
4. Zero Accountability Culture – Delays in prosecution, withdrawal of charges, foreign escapes (Golden Visas, anyone?) — all fuel public rage.
5. Fake News Defense Tactics – When caught, some players cry “political persecution” or flood social media with misinformation.
6. Institutional Collapse – The Sandiganbayan’s staggered raffling of Co’s cases into 3 different divisions? Classic fragmentation — harder to consolidate evidence, harder to convict.
PART V: WHAT MUST BE DONE — REFORM, JUSTICE, TRUTH
🔥 Legal Fixes:
Full Asset Recovery: Freeze accounts, trace overseas holdings, and seize ill-gotten wealth.
Public Procurement Overhaul: Mandatory transparency, public access to documents, blockchain tracking.
Whistleblower Rewards: Cash incentives, protection, and anonymity.
Biblical Integrity Training for Officials: Yes, really. Proverbs 10:9 — “Whoever walks in integrity walks securely.”

PART VI: A SECRET YOU MUST KNOW

Did you know that many of these contracts are recycled? The same names show up across DOH, DepEd, DPWH, even LGUs. The fixers use front companies, dummy bidders, and bribed insiders. It's a national syndicate dressed as public service.
And guess who pays the price? You. The taxpayers. The teachers. The sick. The students.
But now you know.
CONCLUSION: THE TRUTH IS OUT

You now hold the truth. Facts, documents, timelines. We’ve exposed the corruption behind Pharmally, the overpriced DepEd laptops, the flood-control scams, and their ties to political powerbrokers like Zaldy Co.
So now the choice is yours. Will you believe fake news? Or will you share the truth?
We’ve done our part. We’ve given you the facts. If you keep believing disinformation after this, the lie is no longer theirs — it’s yours.
